Augustus.text: Call's talkative, educated partner in the Hat Creek outfit and a former Ranger, Gus tracked Blue Duck across the plains, wiped out the gang holding Lorena, and has been nursing her back to health in a tent trailing the herd. In Kansas he joined Call's posse after the dying Wilbarger, helped hang the horsethieves, Jake among them, and is now driving the recovered horses back toward the herd.

Pea Eye.text: A loyal, slow-spoken Hat Creek hand and veteran of Call's Ranger days, half deaf from an old Indian fight. After the long drive from Lonesome Dove through Indian Territory into Kansas, he rode with Call, Gus, Deets and Newt after Wilbarger's killers, helped hang the Suggs gang and Jake, and is now herding the recovered horses west across the prairie toward the cattle.

Call.text: The stern, driven captain of the Hat Creek outfit and Gus's partner, set on beating everyone to Montana's best grass. After crossing the Arkansas he left Dish in charge of the herd and rode out to the dying Wilbarger. He tracked the horsethieves and hanged the Suggs gang along with his old comrade Jake, and is now driving the recovered horses back west toward his herd.

Newt.text: The youngest Hat Creek hand, raised around the outfit after his mother Maggie's death, eager to prove himself a man on the drive to Montana. He has survived stampedes, Sean's death, and losing his way in Kansas, and his horse Mouse was gored to death. Now he rides with Call's posse, which has just hanged the Suggs gang and Jake, herding the recovered horses back toward the cattle.

Lorena.text: A former Lonesome Dove saloon girl who left town with Jake hoping to reach San Francisco, Lorena was kidnapped by Blue Duck and rescued by Gus, who has cared for her ever since. While Call's posse chases Wilbarger's killers, she stays in her tent near the wagon north of the Arkansas, west of Dodge, watched over by Dish as the herd drifts north.

Lippy.text: The Dry Bean's piano player, who joined the drive with Augustus and now helps with the horses and wagon, still nervous of snakes since the Nueces and once crushed under the overturned wagon. He claims an Apache gave him the hole in his stomach. With Call and Gus away, he stays with Dish's crew and Lorena, the herd bedded a day's drive north of the Arkansas.

Dish Boggett.text: The outfit's top hand, a proud Matagorda cowboy hopelessly in love with Lorena since Lonesome Dove. North of the Arkansas, Call has left him in charge of the herd and of Lorena while the captain chases horsethieves. Dish brings her meals and keeps sleepless watch by her tent, daydreaming about Montana, as the cattle ease north about a day past the river, west of Dodge.

Deets.text: Call's steady, trusted scout, a veteran of the Ranger years who finds the safe river crossings, reads tracks, and quietly longs for home. Called away from the herd after the Arkansas crossing, he followed Wilbarger's killers, picked out Jake's track among the thieves, and saw them caught and hanged. He is now helping drive the recovered horses west at night toward the herd.

Jake Spoon.text: A charming, drifting ex-Ranger who fled an accidental killing in Fort Smith, brought Lorena north, then abandoned her and took up gambling. Riding with the Suggs brothers, he saw them murder Wilbarger's men and two farmers and steal horses, and he shot a man himself at Doan's Store. Call's posse caught the gang at a Kansas creek and hanged him with the others; he lies buried on its slope.

July Johnson.text: The young sheriff of Fort Smith, sent after Jake, whose quest collapsed after his wife Elmira ran off and Joe, Roscoe and Janey were killed on the Canadian. After his horse died he walked to a trail herd, bought another, and reached Dodge City. Learning that Elmira's old man Dee Boot is alive, he has ridden out alone at night to keep searching for her.

Chick.text: One of Wilbarger's hands, who came with him to Lonesome Dove to buy horses and recovered stock early in the story. Months later, camped north of the Arkansas with Wilbarger's horse herd, he was killed in a night raid by the Suggs gang. Call's posse later found his scavenged remains on a Kansas knoll and buried them.

Wilbarger.text: A Yale-educated trail boss who bought horses from Call in Lonesome Dove, later told July that Jake was coming north, and kindly supplied Gus and Lorena with a tent and food on the Canadian. Driving horses north of the Arkansas, he was robbed and shot three times by the Suggs gang. He died beside the river talking with Call and Gus, who buried him under a buffalo skull.

Allen O'Brien.text: An Irishman found lost and starving in Mexico with his brother Sean, who signed on with the Hat Creek drive though he pines for his young wife back in Ireland. He lost Sean to water moccasins at the Nueces crossing. He has kept on as a hand through Fort Worth, Indian Territory and the Canadian, singing Irish songs at camp as the herd pushes north.

Jasper Fant.text: A nervous cowboy from up the Rio Grande, hired in Lonesome Dove, who constantly frets about drowning in the rivers ahead. He has come through the stampedes, the Canadian hailstorm crossing and the grasshopper plains with the herd. With Call away chasing horsethieves, he stays with Dish's crew north of the Arkansas, west of Dodge, where the cattle are bedded.

Bill Spettle.text: The elder of two barefoot boys from a poor widow's farm near Pickles Gap, hired by Call for the drive. He worked the herd through the brush country and past San Antonio. Crossing the empty grassland of Indian Territory, he was struck dead by lightning in a storm that also killed thirteen cattle, and was hastily buried on the muddy plain.

Ben Rainey.text: One of Maude Rainey's many sons, promised to Call as a hand along with his brother Jimmy. A green cowboy who worried about drowning in the Red River, he has made it with the herd through Indian Territory and into Kansas. He now stays with Dish's crew north of the Arkansas while Call's party chases the horsethieves.

Needle Nelson.text: A hand from north of San Antonio who joined the outfit during the branding and has worried since about how many rivers lie between them and the Yellowstone. He has helped push the herd through Fort Worth, across the Red and the hail-lashed Canadian, and into Kansas. He was last with the crew just south of the Arkansas crossing near Dodge.

Bert Borum.text: A cheerful cowboy from Brownsville hired on during the branding near Lonesome Dove. He has come with the herd past Austin and Fort Worth, across the Red and the Canadian, wondering whether the treeless plains reach all the way to Canada. With Call away after the horsethieves, he remains with Dish's crew and Lorena just north of the Arkansas, west of Dodge.

Soupy Jones.text: A hand who turned up at the herd camp the morning the drive began, freshly widowed in Bastrop, and was hired on the spot. He has stuck with the herd through Texas, Indian Territory and the grasshopper-stripped plains of Kansas. He now rides with Dish's crew guarding the cattle and Lorena about a day's drive north of the Arkansas.

Joe.text: A boy from July's Fort Smith household whom Elmira insisted ride along when July went after Jake, though she was quietly plotting to leave. He shared July's long search through Texas, met Wilbarger, and joined up with Roscoe and Janey. Left waiting at a canyon-mouth camp on the Canadian while July and Gus attacked Blue Duck's gang, he was killed by a night intruder and buried there.

Elmira.text: July's restless wife, a former Kansas prostitute who slipped away from Fort Smith while pregnant, rode a whiskey boat up the Arkansas, then crossed the plains on Big Zwey's hide wagon. Reaching Clara's ranch on the North Platte exhausted, she gave birth to a boy, then left him there and set out by night for Ogallala with Zwey and Luke, hoping to find Dee Boot.

Roscoe Brown.text: July's reluctant deputy, pushed by Fort Smith to ride after the sheriff with word that Elmira had fled. Along the way the runaway Janey joined him, and July rescued them from robbers near Fort Worth, after which they travelled north together. Left at a camp on the Canadian with Joe and Janey while July went after Blue Duck, he was killed in the night.

Big Zwey.text: A big buffalo hunter on the whiskey boat who killed a trader in a fight over Elmira and offered to take her to Ogallala. From Bent's Fort he brought her across the plains by hide wagon, and smashed Luke's head against a wheel for harassing her. After her stop at Clara's ranch, he is driving her by night toward Ogallala, twenty miles off.

Janey.text: A resourceful runaway girl who joined Roscoe on the road, doctored his stings, caught his food, and pelted robbers with rocks until July arrived. Refusing to be left in Fort Worth, she followed the party north on foot. While July and Gus attacked Blue Duck's camp, she waited at the canyon-mouth camp on the Canadian, where she was killed by a night intruder.

Po Campo.text: The odd new cook who walked into the outfit's camp past Austin with a donkey and quickly won the crew with unusual dishes. He once raised sheep on the Llano Estacado until Blue Duck killed his three sons. North of the Arkansas, he stays with Dish's crew and has befriended Lorena, bringing her wild plums from a creek he says carries snowmelt from the Rockies.

Luke.text: A buffalo hunter in Big Zwey's hide outfit who won money at cards at the fort where Elmira joined them. Crossing northern Kansas, he harassed her until Zwey slammed his head against a wagon wheel. He is still with them after they stopped at Clara's ranch on the Platte, now riding by night toward Ogallala, about twenty miles away.

Roy Suggs.text: One of the Suggs brothers, outlaws who drew Jake along north from Dallas while they plotted robbery and murder. With his brothers he raided Wilbarger's camp, killed his men, and murdered two Kansas farmers before heading toward Nebraska with stolen horses. Call's posse caught the gang camped at a Kansas creek and hanged them there.

Dan Suggs.text: The ruthless leader of the Suggs brothers, who lured Jake into their gang and boasted that no Kansas lawman could catch him. He led the raid on Wilbarger's horse camp, personally murdered two plowing farmers and hanged and burned their bodies, and drove the stolen horses north. Call's posse captured the gang at a creek camp and hanged them.

Frog Lip.text: A rough member of the Suggs gang who rode north from Dallas with Jake and wrecked a German farmer's sod house by running his cows through the roof. During the gang's night raid on Wilbarger's camp north of the Arkansas, he was gut-shot, and Eddie Suggs finished him off.

Eddie Suggs.text: The youngest of the Suggs brothers, riding north with Jake and the gang through Indian Territory and Kansas. In the raid on Wilbarger's camp he finished off the gut-shot Frog Lip, then helped drive the stolen horses and mules toward Nebraska. Call's posse caught up with the gang at their creek camp and hanged them.

Clara.text: The woman Augustus once loved and proposed to in Austin, who instead married the Kentucky horse trader Bob Allen and followed him to a ranch on the North Platte in Nebraska. With Bob now lying paralyzed, she runs the place herself. When the exhausted stranger Elmira arrived, gave birth and slipped away by night, Clara was left caring for both Bob and the newborn boy.
